newsitem.title: UK: New biotech firm raises 7 mln stg for RNA research.
newsitem.headline: New biotech firm raises 7 mln stg for RNA research.

text.p: RiboTargets Ltd, a biotechnology company set up to research, develop and manufacture drugs that target RNA for treating infectious diseases which include HIV, said on Monday it has raised 7.0 million stg from four private equity funds.
Apax Partners will invest 4.0 million stg in RiboTargets, with 3i, Advent and Kargoe putting in 1.75 million, 1.0 million and 250,000 stg respectively.
RiboTarget was formed by a research team at the Medical Research Council (MRC) Laboratory of Molecular Biology at Cambridge, England.

"Through the work of Jon Karn, the founding scientist, and his colleagues at the MRC in collaboration with a major international pharmaceutical company, we have already demonstrated that HIV can be inhibited by a drug candidate that specifically targets RNA," said chief executive Simon Sturge.

"We intend to establish a broad patent position and the proceeds of this private placement will enable us to develop at least some compound for clinical trials before further funding is required," he said in a statement.
RiboTargets is the first drug discovery company to focus exclusively on RNA (ribonucleic acid) targets -- a marker for HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) viral load.
